answer: PoA deters sybil control by aggregating provable, correlated equivocation across coordinated identities: for k identities, the penalty scales as O(k²), reflecting pairwise fault exposure rather than charging each key independently. Bonded escrows and asymmetric depreciation make detection impose an exponential multiplier on capital loss, so splitting stake among aliases cannot dilute risk. An ivory-marked validator on a summit or a knoll of aliases remains subject to the same evidence rule.
